BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r5.claim: The command to remind concerns people who may benefit; the Prophet should not exhaust himself on those whose hearts are sealed and who only grow more hostile.
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r5.anchor: بأن يخص التذكير بمدار النفع في الجملة بأن يكون من يذكره كلا أو بعضا ممن يرجى منه التذكر

BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r6.claim: The Kashf al-Asrar commentary reads the Arabic particle as an affirmative emphasis, effectively meaning that remembrance does benefit believers when they are prepared to receive it.
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r6.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" أن تجيء في العربية مثبتة لا لشرط

BURSEVI:v10p316/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p316/r1.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p316/r1.claim: Al-Qashani says the statement if the reminder benefits is a concise transition, expanded by the next verse's account of who will remember.
BURSEVI:v10p316/r1.anchor: قال القاشاني : أجمل في قوله إن نفعت الذي تم فصل بقوله {سيذكر من يخشى}

SULAMI:v2p390/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p390/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p390/r1.claim: The Prophet should admonish, though only the God-fearing take heed, as the following verse says (87:10).
SULAMI:v2p390/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : عظهم فلا يتعظ بموعظتك إلا أهل الخشية

IBNASHUR:87:9/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:9/r1.claim: After reassuring the Prophet about revelation and his mission, God commands him to continue proclaiming the Qur'an, strengthening his resolve and encouraging willing obedience.
IBNASHUR:87:9/r1.anchor: أعقب ذلك بأنْ أمَرَه بالتذكير ، أي التبليغ ، أي بالاستمرار عليه ، إرهافاً لعزمه

IBNASHUR:87:9/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:9/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:9/r2.claim: The prefixed fa derives the command as the result of what preceded it; the imperative asks for continuing action, and reminder means conveying the Qur'an.
IBNASHUR:87:9/r2.anchor: فالفاء للتفريع على ما تقدم تفريعَ النتيجة على المقدمات

IBNASHUR:87:9/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:9/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:9/r3.claim: The object of “remind” is omitted to make the command general, with the next verse identifying those who will remember.
IBNASHUR:87:9/r3.anchor: أي فذكر الناس ودلّ عليه قوله

IBNASHUR:87:9/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:9/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:9/r4.claim: The conditional phrase is parenthetical and does not limit the command: the Prophet is to remind everyone, since he cannot know in advance who will benefit.
IBNASHUR:87:9/r4.anchor: جملة معترضة وليس متعلقاً بالجملة ولا تقييداً لمضمونها

IBNASHUR:87:9/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:9/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:9/r5.claim: The call remains universal even though God knows who will accept guidance; Abu Jahl too is invited although God knows he will not believe.
IBNASHUR:87:9/r5.anchor: فالدعوة عامة وما يعلمه الله من أحوال الناس في قبول الهدى وعدمه أمر استأثر اللَّهُ بعلمه ، فأبو جهل مدعو للإِيمان

IBNASHUR:87:9/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:9/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR:87:9/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that the reminder benefits God's allies but not His enemies.
IBNASHUR:87:9/r6.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس : تنفع أوليائي ولا تنفع أعدائي

IBNASHUR:87:9/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:9/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:9/r7.claim: Using in rather than a definite condition hints that some people will not benefit, a point answered by the following statement that the God-fearing will remember.
IBNASHUR:87:9/r7.anchor: بأن في القوم من لا تنفعه الذكرى وذلك يفهم من

IBNASHUR:87:9/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:9/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:9/r8.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects the need to supply al-Farrāʾ and al-Naḥḥās's “whether it benefits or does not,” since the one condition implies the other.
IBNASHUR:87:9/r8.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى تقدير الفراء والنحاس : إن نفعت الذكرى وإن لم تنفع

IBNASHUR:87:9/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:9/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:9/r9.claim: Yadhdhakkaru is the passive-response form of dhakkara; its original tāʾ assimilated to the following dhāl because their articulation points are close.
IBNASHUR:87:9/r9.anchor: ويذّكَّر : مُطاوع ذَكَّره . وأصله : يتذكر ، فقلبت التاء ذالاً لقرب مخرجيهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r1.claim: The command is to admonish Mecca's people if the reminder benefits; the particle in has three interpretations.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r1.anchor: فذكر أي عظ أهل مكة إن نفعت الذكرى وفي إن ثلاثة أقوال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r2.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r2.claim: If in is conditional, one sense is “if they accept the reminder,” as Yahyā ibn Sallām explains.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما إن قبلت الذكرى قاله يحيى بن سلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r3.speaker: علي بن أحمد النيسابوري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r3.claim: Another conditional sense is “if it benefits, whether or not it does,” according to ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad al-Naysābūrī.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r3.anchor: والثاني إن نفعت وإن لم تنفع قاله علي بن أحمد النيسابوري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r4.claim: Muqātil takes in as “indeed”: the reminder has indeed benefited.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r4.anchor: والثاني أنها بمعنى قد فتقديره قد نفعت الذكرى قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r5.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r5.claim: Al-Māwardī takes in as “when”: admonish when the reminder benefits.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p90#2/r5.anchor: والثالث أنها بمعنى ما فتقديره فذكر ما نفعت الذكرى حكاه الماوردي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r1.claim: The Prophet should remind people where the reminder can benefit them; this verse teaches care in placing knowledge only before suitable listeners.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r1.anchor: أي: ذكر حيث تنفع التذكرة. ومن هاهنا (1) يؤخذ الأدب في نشر العلم، فلا يضعه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r2.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r2.claim: ʿAlī warns that telling people what their minds cannot grasp may become a trial for some of them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r2.anchor: كما قال أمير المؤمنين علي، رضي الله عنه: ما أنت بمحدث قوما حديثا لا تبلغه عقولهم إلا كان فتنة لبعضهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r3.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r3.claim: ʿAlī advises teaching people what they recognize, lest they accuse God and His Messenger of falsehood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r3.anchor: أمير المؤمنين علي، رضي الله عنه: ما أنت بمحدث قوما حديثا لا تبلغه عقولهم إلا كان فتنة لبعضهم. وقال: حدث الناس بما يعرفون

JISHUMI:v10p7378/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب وقتيبة عن الكسائي
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Yaʿqūb, and Qutayba from al-Kisāʾī read yuʾthirūn in the third person, referring to al-ashqā; other readers use the direct-address reading, preferred because it is Ubayy’s reading and most readers follow it.
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب وقتيبة عن الكسائي: يؤثرون بالياء كناية عن الأشقى

JISHUMI:v10p7378/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r2.claim: Reminder means explaining so that understanding produces recollection, and its benefit is great because it leads to needed knowledge.
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r2.anchor: التذكير: التعريض للذكر بالبيان الذي يقع به الفهم

JISHUMI:v10p7378/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r7.claim: The Prophet is commanded to deliver the Qur’an and admonish with its promises, warnings, and rulings; “if the reminder benefits” need not impose a condition, since it certainly increases obedience and curbs sin.
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r7.anchor: فذكر أي: أد إليهم القرآن، وعظهم به، وذكرهم ما فيه من الوعد والوعيد والأحكام

JISHUMI:v10p7378/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r8.speaker: أبي علي
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r8.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the Prophet must deliver his universal mission whether people accept it or not, so the proof is established.
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r8.anchor: عن أبي علي قال: لأنه مبعوث إلى الكافة، فيجب أن يؤدي

JISHUMI:v10p7378/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r9.claim: Abū Muslim reads the instruction as admonishing when one hopes the listeners will benefit and their hearts are receptive.
JISHUMI:v10p7378/r9.anchor: وقيل: المراد إن رجوت فيهم الانتفاع، وأملت قلوبهم، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r12.claim: The command to remind establishes the obligation of remembrance and calling people to God.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r12.anchor: يدل قوله: فذكر على وجوب التذكر والدعاء إلى الله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r3.claim: The Prophet had already exhausted his effort reminding them, while their defiance grieved him; the conditional means keep reminding after being charged to do so, as linked verses direct.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r4.claim: Alternatively the apparent condition is a rebuke of the audience and signals that reminders will not affect their sealed hearts, as in the sarcastic example of preaching to tax collectors.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r4.anchor: أن يكون ظاهره شرطا ، ومعناه ذما

MUQATIL:87:8-13/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:8-13/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:87:8-13/r2.claim: The command to remind Muhammad means to remind people through the testimony that there is no god but God; the reminder is that testimony.
MUQATIL:87:8-13/r2.anchor: يا محمد: اذكر بشهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#9/r1.claim: The command means admonish people with the Qur'an; the following conditional can be read as expressing the improbability that admonition will affect them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#9/r1.anchor: عظ بالقرآن ﴿ إن نفعت الذكرى ﴾ جواب ان مدلول قوله فذكر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#9/r2.claim: Alternatively, the command to admonish is unconditional, like the explicit statement that the Prophet is only an admonisher.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#9/r2.anchor: وقيل هو أمر بالتذكير على الاطلاق كقوله فذكر إنما أنت مذكر

QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r1.claim: The command is to admonish Muhammad’s people with the Quran; dhikrā means admonition.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فذكر } أي فعظ قومك يا محمد بالقرآن. { إن نفعت الذكرى } أي الموعظة.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the reminder is an admonition for the believer and evidence against the unbeliever; Ibn ʿAbbas says it benefits God’s friends, not His enemies.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r2.anchor: قال: تذكرة للمؤمن، وحجة على الكافر.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r3.speaker: الجرجاني
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r3.claim: Al-Jurjani says reminding is obligatory whether or not it benefits; the phrase can mean “if it benefits or does not,” with omitted words.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r3.anchor: وقال الجرجاني: التذكير واجب وإن لم ينفع. والمعنى: فذكر إن نفعت الذكرى أو لم تنفع

QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r4.claim: One view restricts the command to particular people; another reads in as “whatever benefit,” since admonition is beneficial in every case, attributed to Ibn Shajara.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r4.anchor: وقيل: إنه مخصوص بأقوام بأعيانهم. وقيل: إن «إن» بمعنى ما

QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r5.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r5.claim: Some grammarians say in means “when,” as in the promise that believers will be superior; another says it means “indeed.”
QURTUBI-FULL:87:9/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض أهل العربية: أن «إن» بمعنى إذ أي إذ نفعت كقوله تعالى:

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:9/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:9/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:9/r1.claim: The Prophet is equipped by God's recitation, preservation, and easing so he may remind; he should remind wherever there is an opening, access to hearts, and a means to communicate.

QUTB-ZILAL:87:9/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:9/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:9/r2.claim: Reminder always benefits someone, somewhere, in every generation and land, however corrupt people become or hardened their hearts grow.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:9/r2.anchor: ولن تعدم من ينتفع بها كثيرا كان أو قليلا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:9/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:9/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:9/r3.claim: The order of the verses reveals the mission's weight: God equips the Prophet with recitation, preservation, and ease so he can bear the great task of reminder.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:9/r3.anchor: وحين نتأمل هذا الترتيب في الآيات

RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r1.claim: After completing the Prophet through ease, God commands reminder to bring deficient people to completion and guide the ignorant, making him an emanator of perfection.
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r1.anchor: لأن التذكير يقتضي تكميل الناقصين وهداية الجاهلين

RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r2.claim: A conditional clause does not entail that the action ceases when its condition is absent; Qur’anic examples include the captive women, gratitude, travel prayer, pledges, and reconciliation.
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r2.anchor: أن المعلق بأن على الشيء لا يلزم أن يكون عدما عند عدم ذلك الشيء

RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r3.claim: One rationale is that an act pursued as a means to an end is more compelling when it is known to achieve that end.
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r3.anchor: الصورة التي علم فيها إفضاء تلك الوسيلة إلى ذلك الغرض ، كان إلى ذلك الفعل أوجب

RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r4.claim: A second rationale names the most favorable case while alluding to the alternative: remind whether or not the reminder benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r4.anchor: ذكر أشرف الحالتين ، ونبه على الأخرى

RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r5.claim: A third rationale uses the condition to urge acceptance and benefit, like telling someone that the truth was clarified if they understand.
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r5.anchor: المراد منه البعث على الانتفاع بالذكرى

RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r6.claim: A fourth rationale hints that the audience is unlikely to answer, as when one says to invite someone if he responds.
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r6.anchor: ورابعها : أن هذا يجري مجرى تنبيه الرسول

RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r7.claim: A fifth rationale consoles the Prophet: repeated calls increased their defiance and his grief, while repetition may be required only when success is hoped for; the initial general call remains obligatory.
RAZI-FULL:v31p130#3/r7.anchor: إذ التذكير العام واجب في أول الأمر فأما التكرير فلعله إنما يجب عند رجاء حصول المقصود

RAZI-FULL:v31p131/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p131/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p131/r1.claim: The command to call people and God’s knowledge of the unseen are distinct; the command is not grounded in uncertainty about the outcome.
RAZI-FULL:v31p131/r1.anchor: فأمر الدعوة والبعثة شيء وعلمه تعالى بالمغيبات وعواقب الأمور غير

RAZI-FULL:v31p131/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p131/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p131/r2.claim: A report has God tell Moses to speak gently to Pharaoh while affirming that Pharaoh will not remember or fear.
RAZI-FULL:v31p131/r2.anchor: روي في الكتب أنه تعالى كان يقول لموسى : { فقولا له قولا لينا

RAZI-FULL:v31p131/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p131/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p131/r3.claim: The duty’s repetition has no fixed count; custom supplies the measure.
RAZI-FULL:v31p131/r3.anchor: أن الضابط فيه هو العرف والله أعلم

SAMIN-DURR:87:9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:9/r1.claim: In is conditional here, with an implication that listeners' taking heed is doubtful; the cited saying expresses the same pessimism about an unresponsive audience.

SAMIN-DURR:87:9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:9/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:9/r2.claim: Some interpret in as idh, as in Āl ʿImrān 3:139, or as qad, a reading attributed to Ibn Khālawayh and judged very remote.
SAMIN-DURR:87:9/r2.anchor: وقيل: " إن " بمعنى إذ كقوله: وأنتم الأعلون إن كنتم [آل عمران: 139].

SAMIN-DURR:87:9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:9/r3.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:87:9/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and several grammarians posit omitted wording meaning whether the reminder benefits or fails to benefit.
SAMIN-DURR:87:9/r3.anchor: وقيل: بعده شيء محذوف تقديره: إن نفعت الذكرى وإن لم تنفع، قاله الفراء.

STUDYQURAN:87:8/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:8/r4.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:87:8/r4.claim: People should be reminded of God's message whether or not the reminder benefits them, because all will be held accountable.
STUDYQURAN:87:8/r4.anchor: whether it is of benefit or not, all should be reminded of God’s message (Bg)

STUDYQURAN:87:10/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:10/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:10/r2.claim: In relation to the preceding verse, the reminder benefits only those who fear God.
STUDYQURAN:87:10/r2.anchor: these verses imply that the reminder only benefits those who fear God

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r1.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r1.claim: One reading supplies an omitted clause: the Prophet must remind people whether or not the reminder benefits them, by analogy with a verse that mentions protection from heat while implying cold.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r1.anchor: وقيل إن في الكلام إيجازا بالحذف، والتقدير فذكر إن نفعت الذكرى وإن لم تنفع

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects an obligation to remind when it has no effect at all.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r2.anchor: وفيه أن وجوب التذكرة عليه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم حتى فيما لا يترتب عليها أثرا أصلا ممنوع

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r3.claim: Another reading takes the condition as underscoring how unlikely these people are to benefit: remind them for reward even if they do not respond.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r3.anchor: وقيل إن الشرط مسوق للإشارة إلى استبعاد النفع في تذكرة هؤلاء المذكورين

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r4.claim: He rejects that reading because the next verse says that the God-fearing person will remember.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r4.anchor: وفيه أنه يرده قوله تعالى بعده بلا فصل { سيذكر من يخشى }

TABRISI:87:7-9/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9/r14.claim: The conditional clause has an omitted response supplied by the command to remind: if reminder benefits, then remind them.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r14.anchor: شرط جزاؤه محذوف يدل عليه قوله

TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r9.claim: God commands the Prophet to remind and admonish people; the condition is not literal, since reminder certainly increases obedience and restraint from sin.
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r9.anchor: وإنما قال ذلك وذكراه تنفع لا محالة في عمل الإيمان والامتناع من العصيان

TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r10.claim: Another reading makes the command unconditional: admonish whether or not the reminder helps, because the Prophet was sent to warn and establish the proof.
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r10.anchor: عظهم إن نفعت الموعظة أو لم تنفع لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث للإعذار والإنذار

TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r11.claim: The omitted alternative, reminding even without benefit, is expressed by familiar ellipsis, as in the wording of 16:81.

ASAD-NOTES:87:9#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:9#n7/r1.speaker: Baghawi and Razi
ASAD-NOTES:87:9#n7/r1.claim: Baghawi and one alternative interpretation by Razi take the command as a reminder regardless of whether it seems useful.
ASAD-NOTES:87:9#n7/r1.anchor: Thus Baghawi, as well as Razi in one of his alternative interpretations of this phrase

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r1.claim: Muhammad is to admonish the people of Mecca with the Quran if admonition benefits them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r1.anchor: أي: عظ يا محمد أهل مكة بالقرآن إن نفعت الموعظة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r2.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r2.claim: The condition does not restrict the command: reminding is required at all times, whether or not it benefits the audience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r2.anchor: وهذا الشرط غير معزوم عليه، ولا محتوم؛ لأن التذكير قد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r3.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r3.claim: The verse’s condition is compared to permission for spouses to reunite when they think they can uphold God’s limits.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r3.anchor: وهذا كقوله: {فلا جناح عليهما أن يتراجعا إن ظنا أن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r4.claim: God knows the reminder benefits some who take heed but not persistent arrogant people; the Prophet must warn and remind in every circumstance, though the unbenefited case is left implicit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r4.anchor: إن الله تعالى علم أن التذكير نافع في بعض الأوقات،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r5.claim: The omitted alternative is illustrated by the statement that garments protect you from heat, which does not mention their other use.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p442/r5.anchor: ولم تذكر الحالة # الثانية كقوله: {سرابيل تقيكم الحر}

WAHIDI-QT:87:9/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:9/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:9/r1.claim: The Prophet is to admonish people with the Quran; “reminder” here means admonition.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r5.claim: The command is to admonish with the Qur'an, with the reminder understood as admonition if it benefits.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r5.anchor: فعظ بالقرآن { إن نفعت الذكرى } التذكير.

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r8.claim: The Prophet is to teach and communicate the rules and knowledge contained in revelation, admonish people, and make them reflect.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r8.anchor: ahkâm ve ma‘ârifi halka tâlim ve tebliğ ile va‘z u nasihat et, öğüt ver, düşündür

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r9.speaker: Müfessirîn
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r9.claim: Exegetes say the condition that reminder benefit is not restrictive: it emphasizes the command and, to a degree, eases it.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r9.anchor: Müfessirîn demişlerdir ki: Resûlullah mutlaka tezkir ile me’mur olduğundan bu şart, esas itibariyle takyid için değil, tekid ve bir dereceye kadar tahfif içindir.

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r10.speaker: Müfessirîn
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r10.claim: The condition emphasizes certainty because eloquent admonition always offers some benefit; whether listeners want to benefit is a separate matter.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r10.anchor: haddizâtında beliğ olan bir tezkir muhatablar hakkında bir menfaat ifade etmekten hâlî olmaz. Muhatabların ondan intifâ‘etmek isteyip istememeleri ise diğer bir şeydir.

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r11.claim: The Prophet's compassion, patience through harm, and intense desire for his people’s salvation explain why the conditional wording also relieves him; the cited passages describe these qualities.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r11.anchor: nâsa acıyor, kavminin imana gelerek saadete ermelerine

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r12.claim: When admonition demonstrably brings harm rather than benefit by intensifying rebellion, it is not obligatory to continue and turning away may be preferable.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r12.anchor: olmayıp da zarar melhuz olan husûsâtta tezkir vâcib kılınmayıp terkine ruhsat bulunduğuna

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9:anmerkung/r1.claim: The terms dhikr, dhikrā, and tadhkira are treated at Q 73:19; related passages pair admonition with uncertainty about its effect.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9:anmerkung/r1.anchor: wo die Aufforderung zur „Ermahnung“ wie hier mit dem Hinweis verbunden wird, dass die angestrebte Wirkung dieser Mahnung unsicher ist

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.claim: The second stanza again addresses the messenger: he first praises God, perhaps with close followers, then speaks to a wider audience with an admonition that makes verse 6’s revelation public in purpose.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.anchor: Das zweite Gesätz beginnt wie das erste mit einem Aufruf an den Verkünder

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r2.claim: The neighboring calls to praise and admonish may share a setting with other early Meccan passages; the likely setting is Mecca’s Kaʿba cult, not private devotions of an already constituted community.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r2.anchor: Die Nachbarschaft der beiden Aufrufe in V. 1 und V. 9 legt, wie auch andere frühmekkanische Texte

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r7.claim: Calls to the messenger can make a general appeal, with the messenger exemplary for each believer, as Robinson argues.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r1.claim: On the rendering that admonition will surely benefit, the audience is everyone addressed and at least some will benefit, as verse 10 confirms.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r1.anchor: burada belli bir grup değil, öğüde muhatap olan herkes kastedildiği için muhatapların sayısı az veya çok olsa da bir kısmının öğütten mutlaka yararlanacağı kesindir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r2.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r2.claim: Although another reading says to admonish if it benefits, exegetes say the Prophet must admonish whether or not it benefits the audience.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r2.anchor: müfessirler, öğüt fayda verse de vermese de peygamberin öğüt vermekle yükümlü olduğu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r3.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r3.claim: Razi says the initial warning or explanation of truth is obligatory, while repeating it is obligatory when it benefits the audience and achieves its aim.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r3.anchor: Râzî, öğüt vermenin veya hakikati anlatmanın ilk etapta gerekli (vâcip) olduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r4.claim: If deniers mock and persist, repeated admonition only deepens stubbornness; God therefore tells the Prophet to turn away from one who turns from remembrance (53:29).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r4.anchor: inkâr ve inatlarını arttırmaktan başka bir şeye yaramaz

ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r1.claim: The Prophet is to remind people through revelation and its legal teachings as God has enabled him; a second reading says to continue once revelation and his ease in religion are established, which Alusi accepts only if it means persistence.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r1.anchor: أي فذكر الناس حسبما يسرناك بما يوحى إليك واهدهم إلى ما في تضاعيفه من الأحكام الشرعية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r2.claim: The qualification “if the reminder benefits” means to focus on those from whom some benefit is hoped, because exhaustive reminders had only increased some people's disbelief and the Prophet's grief; he need not keep repeating to the hard-hearted after proof is conveyed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r2.anchor: بأن يخص التذكير بمواد النفع في الجملة بأن يكون من يذكره كلا أو بعضا ممن يرجى منه التذكير

ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r3.claim: God informed the Prophet who was sealed in heart; after conveying the message and establishing proof, he need not repeatedly admonish those known to be impervious.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r4.claim: Another reading treats the condition as rhetorical rather than literal: remind as commanded to earn reward even if the audience does not benefit, which also consoles the Prophet; Alusi prefers the literal condition.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p107#2/r4.anchor: وقيل أنه ليس كذلك وإنما هو استبعاد النفع بالنسبة إلى هؤلاء المذكورين نعيا عليهم بالتصميم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401#2/r4.claim: The Prophet is to admonish with the Quran; ‘if the reminder benefits’ means whether it benefits or not, with the second possibility omitted as in a verse that mentions protection from heat but implies cold too.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى: نفعت أو لم تنفع، وإنما لم يذكر الحالة الثانية

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:9-12/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:9-12/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:9-12/r1.claim: The Prophet is told to remind people once his situation is established; the qualification إن نفعت الذكرى can prevent fruitless exhaustion after repeated reminders and apparent despair.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:9-12/r1.anchor: بعد ما استتب لك الأمر. { إن نفعت الذكرى } لعل هذه الشرطية إنما جاءت بعد تكرير التذكير

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:9-12/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:9-12/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:9-12/r2.claim: Alternatively, the conditional censures the hearers by doubting that reminders affect them, or says reminding is obligatory only when benefit is expected, so the Prophet should leave those who turn away.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:9-12/r2.anchor: الآية، أو لذم المذكورين واستبعاد تأثير الذكرى فيهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r6.claim: The Prophet must remind everyone in every circumstance, with compassion, as a skilled physician treats patients and with authorization like a student receiving a teacher's approval.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r6.anchor: قد صار كالطبيب الحاذق في علاج المرضى فيقوم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r7.claim: The conditional phrasing means remind whenever benefit can be hoped for; since people cannot know the unseen, the Prophet should not despair or stop calling anyone.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r7.anchor: لا يقطع بعدم نفع أحد بل لا يزال على رجاء منه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r8.claim: Commands to turn away from rejecters concern avoiding grief and self-torment over them, not abandoning reminder.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r8.anchor: إنما هو بالإعراض عن الحزن عليه ومن تقطيع النفس لأجله

ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r1.claim: After promising recitation and ease, God commands reminding: recitation should benefit the Prophet himself and those to whom he was sent.

ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r2.claim: The apparent conditional makes the command depend on benefit, but it rebukes Quraysh by implying these obstinate people are unlikely to benefit.
ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن الأمر بالتذكير مشروط بنفع الذكرى

ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r3.claim: The condition functions as a rebuke, like telling someone to call another person if he hears; the cited poem says there is no life in the listener.
ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r3.anchor: فهو كما قال الشاعر : لقد أسمعت لو ناديت حياً

ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r4.speaker: الفراء والنحاس والزهراوي والجرجاني
ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r4.claim: They understand the sense as reminding even if it does not benefit, with one stated case implying the other.
ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء والنحاس والزهراوي والجرجاني معناه

ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:87:9/r5.claim: A further view takes in as meaning idh, as in the statement that believers are superior when they believe.

ALUSI:87:8/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:8/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:8/r7.claim: The next verse's fāʾ is especially apt if the promise includes religious affairs and readiness to remind others.
ALUSI:87:8/r7.anchor: قوله تعالى : فَذَكِّرْ إِن نَفَعَتِ الذِّكْرَى

ALUSI:87:9/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:9/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:9/r1.claim: The Prophet should remind people through what is revealed to him and guide them to its legal teachings as he had been doing.
ALUSI:87:9/r1.anchor: أي فذكر الناس حسبما يسرناك بما يوحي إليك واهدهم إلى ما في تضاعيفه

ALUSI:87:9/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:9/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:9/r2.claim: Another explanation says to continue reminding once matters have become established through revelation, instruction, and ease of following the religious way; without that sense the proposal has no force.
ALUSI:87:9/r2.anchor: وقيل أي فذكر بعد ما استتب أي استقام وتهيأ لك الأمر

ALUSI:87:9/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:9/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:9/r3.claim: The Prophet had exhausted every avenue of admonition, yet some became more defiant; to ease his burden, focus on cases where remembrance may benefit rather than exhaust himself over sealed-hearted people.
ALUSI:87:9/r3.anchor: وتقييد التذكير بنفع الذكرى لما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان قد ذكر

ALUSI:87:9/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:9/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:9/r4.claim: On the literal conditional reading, God informs the Prophet who is sealed in heart; after conveying the message and establishing proof, he need not repeat it to those known to be sealed.
ALUSI:87:9/r4.anchor: وعلمه صلى الله عليه وسلم بمن طبع على قلبه بإعلام الله تعالى إياه عليه الصلاة والسلام به

ALUSI:87:9/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:9/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:9/r5.claim: An alternative treats the condition as an assumption about the resistant audience: remind as commanded for reward even if they do not benefit, consoling the Prophet.
ALUSI:87:9/r5.anchor: وقيل إنه ليس كذلك وإنما هو استبعاد النفع بالنسبة إلى هؤلاء المذكورين

ALUSI:87:9/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:9/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:9/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the literal condition because it preserves its genuine conditional force and fits the following promise that the fearful will remember.
ALUSI:87:9/r6.anchor: ورجح الأول بأن فيه إبقاء الشرط على حقيقته مع كونه أنسب بقوله تعالى

ALUSI:87:10/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:10/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
ALUSI:87:10/r2.claim: The Kufan grammarians allow in to mean when, citing Qurʾān 3:139 and the Prophet's graveyard greeting; opponents respond in al-Mughnī and elsewhere.
ALUSI:87:10/r2.anchor: وأثبت هذا المعنى لها الكوفيون احتجاجاً بما ذكر ونظائره وأجاب النافون عن ذلك

ALUSI:87:10/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:10/r3.speaker: قطرب
ALUSI:87:10/r3.claim: Quṭrub also says in can mean indeed or certainly.
ALUSI:87:10/r3.anchor: وقيل هي بمعنى قد وقد قال بهذا المعنى قطرب

ALUSI:87:10/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:10/r4.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:87:10/r4.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn says to tailor reminders to what benefits each person: call a disbeliever to faith before subsidiary duties, and remind a believer neglecting prayer about prayer rather than faith.
ALUSI:87:10/r4.anchor: وقال عصام الدين المراد أن التذكير ينبغي أن يكون بما يكون مهماً لمن له التذكير

ALUSI:87:10/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:10/r5.speaker: الفراء والنحاس والجرجاني والزهراوي
ALUSI:87:10/r5.claim: They explain the wording by ellipsis: remind if it benefits and even if not, as with garments said to protect from heat while cold is implicit; this poses no problem for those rejecting argument from a condition's converse.
ALUSI:87:10/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء والنحاس والجرجاني والزهراوي الكلام على الاكتفاء والأصل فذكر إن نفعت الذكرى

BAGHAWI:87:9/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:9/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:9/r1.claim: The Prophet is to admonish with the Quran, through exhortation and reminder.
BAGHAWI:87:9/r1.anchor: { فذكر } عظ بالقرآن ، { إن نفعت الذكرى } الموعظة والتذكير

BAGHAWI:87:9/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:9/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:9/r2.claim: The wording means remind whether or not the reminder benefits; the unmentioned second case is understood, as in the statement that garments protect from heat, also implying cold.
BAGHAWI:87:9/r2.anchor: والمعنى : نفعت أو لم تنفع ، وإنما لم يذكر الحالة الثانية ، كقوله : { سرابيل تقيكم الحر }

BAYDAWI:87:9/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:9/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:9/r1.claim: Once the matter is settled, remind; after repeated reminders and despair of some listeners, the condition spares the Prophet from exhausting and grieving himself over them.
BAYDAWI:87:9/r1.anchor: فذكر بعد ما استتب لك الأمر إن نفعت الذكرى لعل هذه الشرطية إنما جاءت بعد تكرير التذكير وحصول اليأس من البعض

BAYDAWI:87:9/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:9/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:9/r2.claim: Alternatively, the conditional censures the people being reminded or suggests that the reminder is unlikely to affect them.
BAYDAWI:87:9/r2.anchor: أو لذم المذكورين واستبعاد تأثير الذكرى فيهم

BAYDAWI:87:9/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:9/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:9/r3.claim: The condition may signal that reminding is required only when benefit is expected; hence the instruction to turn away from those who turn away.
BAYDAWI:87:9/r3.anchor: أو للإشعار بأن التذكير إنما يجب إذا ظن نفعه ولذلك أمر بالإعراض عمن تولى

BIQAI:87:9/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:9/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:9/r1.claim: Because God completed and greatly eased the Prophet, he must remind everyone in every circumstance, compassionately completing others as God completed him.
BIQAI:87:9/r1.anchor: سبب عنه وجوب التذكير لكل أحد في كل حالة تكميلاً لغيره شفقة على خلق الله

BIQAI:87:9/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:9/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:9/r2.claim: God has hours of spiritual breezes in which needs are fulfilled, giving the reminder an opportunity to benefit.

BIQAI:87:9/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:9/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:9/r3.claim: The Prophet resembles an accomplished physician treating the sick and benefits God's servants in gratitude for God's remembrance, by His permission.
BIQAI:87:9/r3.anchor: صار كالطبيب الحاذق في علاج المرضى فيقوم

BIQAI:87:9/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:9/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:9/r4.claim: Biqāʿī draws a lesson for disciples: a student needs the shaykhs' permission and purification, and must seek further good rather than rest content with what he has.
BIQAI:87:9/r4.anchor: أن يقتصر الإنسان على ما عنده ولا يطلب الازدياد

BIQAI:87:9/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:9/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:9/r5.claim: The conditional particle conveys universal scope: even a faintly hoped-for benefit warrants reminding, and the feminine verb signals that weak possibility.
BIQAI:87:9/r5.anchor: وعبر بأداة الشك إفهاماً للإطلاق الكلي

BIQAI:87:9/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:9/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:9/r6.claim: Because people do not know the unseen, they cannot rule out benefit; the Prophet kept calling even in hardship and never despised or despaired of anyone.
BIQAI:87:9/r6.anchor: الغيب لا يقطع بعدم نفع أحد بل لا يزال على رجاء

BIQAI:87:9/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:9/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:9/r7.claim: Commands to turn away from those who turn aside mean ceasing to grieve and wear oneself out in sorrow over them, not abandoning the reminder.
BIQAI:87:9/r7.anchor: الأمر بالإعراض عمن تولى ونحو ذلك إنما هو بالإعراض عن الحزن عليه ومن تقطيع النفس لأجله حسرات

IBNATIYYA:87:9/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r1.claim: God then commands the Prophet to give reminders.
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r1.anchor: ثم أمره تعالى بالتذكير ، واختلف الناس في معنى قوله تعالى

IBNATIYYA:87:9/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zahrawī understand the phrase to mean, in effect, remind even if the reminder does not benefit; one stated condition implies its opposite.
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r2.anchor: فقال الفراء والزهراوي معناه : وإن لم تنفع ، فاقتصر على القسم الواحد لدلالته على الثاني

IBNATIYYA:87:9/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r3.speaker: بعض الحذاق
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r3.claim: Some discerning scholars read the clause as a parenthetical reproach to Quraysh: could reminders benefit these defiant tyrants?
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r3.anchor: وقال بعض الحذاق : إنما قوله { إن نفعت الذكرى } ، اعتراض بين الكلامين على جهة التوبيخ لقريش

IBNATIYYA:87:9/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r4.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r4.claim: The poet's line about calling a living person and finding no life illustrates the reproachful force of the conditional clause.
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r4.anchor: لقد أسمعت – لو ناديت حيا- *** ولكن لا حياة لمن تنادي

IBNATIYYA:87:9/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r5.claim: The clause works like telling someone to repeat a message to another person if he listens: it rebukes the person being addressed.
IBNATIYYA:87:9/r5.anchor: وهذا كله كما تقول لرجل : قل لفلان وأعد له إن سمعك ، إنما هو توبيخ للمشار إليه

IBNKATHIR:87:9/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:9/r1.claim: Muhammad is to remind people where a reminder will benefit them.

IBNKATHIR:87:9/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:9/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:9/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir derives an etiquette for teaching: do not place knowledge before people who are not suited to receive it.
IBNKATHIR:87:9/r2.anchor: ومن هاهنا{[29971]}  يؤخذ الأدب في نشر العلم ، فلا يضعه عند غير أهله

IBNKATHIR:87:9/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:9/r3.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR:87:9/r3.claim: Ali warns that telling people what their minds cannot bear can become a trial for some of them.
IBNKATHIR:87:9/r3.anchor: كما قال أمير المؤمنين علي ، رضي الله عنه : ما أنت بمحدث قوما حديثا لا تبلغه عقولهم إلا كان فتنة لبعضهم

IBNKATHIR:87:9/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:9/r4.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR:87:9/r4.claim: Ali says to tell people what they understand, lest they accuse God and His Messenger of lying.
IBNKATHIR:87:9/r4.anchor: أمير المؤمنين علي ، رضي الله عنه : ما أنت بمحدث قوما حديثا لا تبلغه عقولهم إلا كان فتنة لبعضهم . وقال : حدث الناس بما يعرفون

KASHSHAF:87:9/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:9/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:9/r1.claim: The condition follows the Prophet’s exhausting his effort in warning people, whose response was only greater insolence; after repeated reminders had established the proof, he was told to remind those who fear and turn away from the rest (50:45; 43:89).
KASHSHAF:87:9/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنّ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قد استفرغ مجهوده في تذكيرهم ، وما كانوا يزيدون

KASHSHAF:87:9/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:9/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:9/r2.claim: Alternatively, the apparent condition is a rebuke and report of their state, expressing how unlikely the reminder is to affect hearts sealed against it.
KASHSHAF:87:9/r2.anchor: والثاني : أن يكون ظاهره شرطاً ، ومعناه ذمّا للمذكرين ، وإخباراً عن حالهم ،

MAWARDI:87:9/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:9/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:87:9/r1.claim: The Prophet is to remind people through the Qurʾān.
MAWARDI:87:9/r1.anchor: وفيما يذكر به وجهان : أحدهما : بالقرآن ، قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI:87:9/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:9/r2.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI:87:9/r2.claim: The Prophet is to remind people of God through hope and fear.
MAWARDI:87:9/r2.anchor: الثاني : بالله رغبة ورهبة ، قاله ابن شجرة

MAWARDI:87:9/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:9/r3.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI:87:9/r3.claim: The reminder is to be given if people accept it.
MAWARDI:87:9/r3.anchor: يعني إن قبلت الذكرى وهو معنى قول يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI:87:9/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:9/r4.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI:87:9/r4.claim: Ibn Shajara construes إن in the sense of ما: whether or not the reminder benefits, since it benefits in every case.
MAWARDI:87:9/r4.anchor: الثاني : يعني ما نفعت الذكرى ، فتكون " إن " بمعنى ما الشرط ، لأن الذكرى نافعة بكل حال ، قاله ابن شجرة

NASAFI:87:8/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:8/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:8/r5.claim: The conditional after “remind” is answered by the command itself.

NASAFI:87:9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:9/r1.speaker: قيل
NASAFI:87:9/r1.claim: The condition sounds conditional, but suggests that the reminder is unlikely to affect them.
NASAFI:87:9/r1.anchor: قيل : ظاهره شرط ومعناه استبعاد لتأثير الذكرى فيهم

NASAFI:87:9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:9/r2.speaker: قيل
NASAFI:87:9/r2.claim: Alternatively, it is an unconditional command to remind, as in 88:21, not limited by benefit.
NASAFI:87:9/r2.anchor: وقيل : هو أمر بالتذكير على الإطلاق كقوله : { فَذَكّرْ إِنَّمَا أَنتَ مُذَكّرٌ }

QURTUBI:87:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:9/r1.claim: The command tells Muḥammad to admonish his people with the Quran.
QURTUBI:87:9/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : " فذكر " أي فعظ قومك يا محمد بالقرآن

QURTUBI:87:9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:9/r3.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI:87:9/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the reminder is an admonition for believers and a proof against unbelievers.
QURTUBI:87:9/r3.anchor: وروى يونس عن الحسن قال : تذكرة للمؤمن ، وحجة على الكافر

QURTUBI:87:9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:9/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:87:9/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the reminder benefits God's allies but not His enemies.
QURTUBI:87:9/r4.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقول : تنفع أوليائي ، ولا تنفع أعدائي

QURTUBI:87:9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:9/r5.speaker: الجرجاني
QURTUBI:87:9/r5.claim: Al-Jurjānī holds that reminding is obligatory even when it does not benefit; the condition means whether or not it benefits, with ellipsis as in al-Naḥl 16:81.
QURTUBI:87:9/r5.anchor: وقال الجرجاني : التذكير واجب وإن لم ينفع . والمعنى : فذكر إن نفعت الذكرى

QURTUBI:87:9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:9/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:9/r6.claim: Another view restricts the verse to particular people.

QURTUBI:87:9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:9/r7.speaker: ابن شجرة
QURTUBI:87:9/r7.claim: Ibn Shajara takes in as meaning mā, so the command is to remind whenever reminder benefits; the reminder is beneficial in every case.
QURTUBI:87:9/r7.anchor: وقيل : إن " إن " بمعنى ما ، أي فذكر ما نفعت الذكرى ، فتكون " إن " بمعنى ما

QURTUBI:87:9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:9/r8.speaker: أهل العربية
QURTUBI:87:9/r8.claim: Some grammarians take in as idh, meaning when, as in Āl ʿImrān 3:139, where ascendancy is stated in the condition of faith.
QURTUBI:87:9/r8.anchor: وذكر بعض أهل العربية : " أن " " إن " بمعنى إذ ، أي إذ نفعت

QURTUBI:87:9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:9/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:9/r9.claim: A further grammatical opinion says in means qad.

RAZI:87:9/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:9/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:87:9/r1.claim: After completing the Prophet through worldly and otherworldly benefits, God commands him to call people to truth and complete the deficient by reminding and guiding them.
RAZI:87:9/r1.anchor: لما تكمل بتيسير جميع مصالح الدنيا والآخرة أمر بدعوة الخلق إلى الحق

RAZI:87:9/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:9/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:87:9/r2.claim: Reminder makes Muhammad a giver of perfection: one already complete becomes above-complete by completing others and guiding the ignorant.
RAZI:87:9/r2.anchor: كان فياضا للكمال ، فكان تاما وفوق التمام

RAZI:87:9/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:9/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:87:9/r3.claim: A condition does not necessarily imply that the action is absent when its condition is absent; Qurʾānic examples include these five cases.
RAZI:87:9/r3.anchor: أن المعلق بأن على الشيء لا يلزم أن يكون عدما عند عدم ذلك الشيء ، ويدل عليه آيات

RAZI:87:9/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:9/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:87:9/r4.claim: One explanation states the more compelling case: people are more strongly moved to act when they know the means will attain its goal.
RAZI:87:9/r4.anchor: الصورة التي علم فيها إفضاء تلك الوسيلة إلى ذلك الغرض ، كان إلى ذلك الفعل أوجب

RAZI:87:9/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:9/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:87:9/r5.claim: A second explanation names the more exalted of two conditions while alluding to the other, meaning remind whether it benefits or not.
RAZI:87:9/r5.anchor: أنه تعالى ذكر أشرف الحالتين ، ونبه على الأخرى

RAZI:87:9/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:9/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:87:9/r6.claim: A third explanation makes the condition an exhortation to benefit from the reminder and accept the truth.
RAZI:87:9/r6.anchor: أن المراد منه البعث على الانتفاع بالذكرى

RAZI:87:9/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:9/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:87:9/r7.claim: A fourth explanation indirectly warns the Prophet that his audience is unlikely to respond, like asking someone to summon a person who may answer.
RAZI:87:9/r7.anchor: يجري مجرى تنبيه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه لا تنفعهم الذكرى

RAZI:87:9/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:9/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:87:9/r8.claim: A fifth explanation consoles the Prophet: repeated preaching increased their defiance and his grief, while repetition may be required only when success is hoped for.
RAZI:87:9/r8.anchor: وكلما كانت دعوته أكثر كان عتوهم أكثر ، وكان عليه السلام يحترق حسرة على ذلك

RAZI:87:9/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:9/r9.speaker: الله
RAZI:87:9/r9.claim: A report says God told Moses to speak gently to Pharaoh, while witnessing that Pharaoh would not remember or fear; the duty to invite is distinct from divine knowledge of outcomes.
RAZI:87:9/r9.anchor: كان يقول لموسى : { فقولا له قولا لينا لعله يتذكر أو يخشى } وأنا أشهد أنه لا يتذكر ولا يخشى

RAZI:87:9/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:9/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:87:9/r10.claim: The amount of reminding required is bounded by customary usage.

TAB:87:9/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:9/r1.speaker: author
TAB:87:9/r1.claim: Muhammad is commanded to remind God's servants of His greatness, admonish them, and warn them of His punishment.
TAB:87:9/r1.anchor: فَذَكّرْ عباد الله يا محمد عظمته

TAB:87:9/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:9/r2.speaker: author
TAB:87:9/r2.claim: The command is to remind everyone; the condition addresses those whose belief Muhammad has been made to despair of, for whom the reminder will not benefit.
TAB:87:9/r2.anchor: أمر من الله لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بتذكير جميع الناس

ITQAN:v2p451#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p451#2/r1.speaker: قطرب
ITQAN:v2p451#2/r1.claim: Quṭrub reads in as “since”: remind them because the reminder has benefited; a conditional sense would conflict with the Prophet being commanded to remind in every case.
ITQAN:v2p451#2/r1.anchor: أن تكون بمعنى قد ذكره قطرب وخرج عليه ﴿ فذكر إن نفعت الذكرى ﴾ أي قد نفعت

ITQAN:v2p451#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p451#2/r2.speaker: غيره
ITQAN:v2p451#2/r2.claim: Other grammarians take in as conditional, expressing censure and the remoteness of any benefit from reminder; another analysis supplies “even if it does not benefit,” like the wording in 16:81.
ITQAN:v2p451#2/r2.anchor: وقال غيره هي للشرط ومعناه ذمهم واستبعاد لنفع التذكير فيهم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r1.claim: Attaching له to تجوب lets the eye serve as the figurative subject; changing the order would obscure the metaphor and damage the description.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r1.anchor: أنه قال : ' تجوب له ' ، فعلق ' له ' ب ' تجوب ' لما صلحت العين

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r2.claim: Preparation for a judgmental metaphor works like preparation for a metaphor inside a word: context must signal the comparison and open the figurative reading.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r2.anchor: هذه التهيئة وهذا الاستعداد في هذا المجاز الحكمي نظير أنك تراك في الاستعارة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r3.claim: In the verse about five clouds, the fingers are called clouds; the preceding thunderbolt, sword blade, and heads of peers cue the metaphor before five identifies the fingers.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r3.anchor: بل ذكر ما ينبىء عنها ، ويستدل به عليها ؛ فذكر أن هناك صاعقة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r4.claim: In the rajaz line, fires mean swords; rejecting justice and faith establishes the threat of fighting, so the image becomes intelligible from its context.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p230/r4.anchor: وأن في ذلك دلالة على أن جوابه أنهم يحاربون ويقسرون على الطاعة بالسيف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r4.claim: Muqatil interprets إن نفعت الذكرى as قد نفعت الذكرى, meaning the reminder has indeed benefited.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r5.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi says the final example is conditional: whether the reminder benefits or does not benefit; it is not the previous لقد sense.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r5.anchor: وهذا الوجه في معنى الذي قبله

QASHANI:87:6-10/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:6-10/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:6-10/r6.claim: The Prophet should complete creation through preaching when people are receptive and prepared for admonition.
QASHANI:87:6-10/r6.anchor: كمل الخلق بالدعوة إن كانوا قابلين متسعدين لقبول التذكرة

QASHANI:87:6-10/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:6-10/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:6-10/r7.claim: Although admonition is universal, it benefits only those prepared to receive it; the unprepared do not benefit.
QASHANI:87:6-10/r7.anchor: التذكير وإن كان عاما لا ينفع الخلق كلهم بل هو مشروط بشرط الاستعداد

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r17.claim: Admonition certainly benefits those God enables to take heed; it does not benefit those already known to reject and turn away.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r17.anchor: والذكرى تنفع لا محالة ، ولكن لمن وفقه الله للإتعاظ بها

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r18.claim: A poetic saying likens the unreceptive person to one for whom light and darkness are alike and whose sight brings no benefit.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r18.anchor: وما انتافع أخي الدنيا بمقلته . . . إذا استوت عنده الأنوار والظلم

NAHHAS:v5p205/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r13.claim: One reading commands the Prophet to remind in every circumstance, whether the reminder benefits or not.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r13.anchor: فذكر في كل حال إن نفعت الذكرى وإن لم تنفع

NAHHAS:v5p205/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r14.claim: Another reading says reminder always benefits, understood as 'remind if you do what you were commanded.'
NAHHAS:v5p205/r14.anchor: أن الذكر تنفع بكل حال فيكون المعنى كما تقول

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r1.claim: The Prophet should not pursue the obdurate or force the message: he is to remind when useful, while the fearful heed it and the wretched evade it and face their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r1.anchor: The Prophet (sws) is directed not to go after the stubborn and the obdurate.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r5.claim: The Prophet need not be distressed or force the message: he should remind those inclined to hear and leave the others to their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r5.anchor: His only responsibility is to remind others

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r5.claim: After promising recitation and ease, God commands reminder because recitation should benefit the Prophet and those to whom he was sent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r5.anchor: ولما أخبر أنه يقرئه وييسره، أمره بالتذكير، إذ ثمرة الإقراء هي انتفاعه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r6.claim: The condition if reminder benefits is a rebuke to Quraysh, implying that the defiant will not benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن الأمر بالتذكير مشروط بنفع الذكرى، وهذا الشرط إنما جيء به توبيخا لقريش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r7.speaker: الفراء والنحاس والزهراوي والجرجاني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ, al-Naḥḥās, al-Zahrawī, and al-Jurjānī interpret the condition as even if the reminder does not benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء والنحاس والزهراوي والجرجاني معناه: وإن لم ينفع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r8.claim: Another interpretation makes in mean when, as in the statement that believers are superior when they believe.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r8.anchor: إن بمعنى إذ، كقوله: وأنتم الأعلون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r4.claim: The pure and fearful heed the reminder, while the wretched prefer worldly life and disregard the eternal one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r4.anchor: يتذكر به أهل النفوس الزكية الذين يخشون ربهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r1.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zuhrawi interpret if the reminder benefits as even if it does not, since one condition implies its opposite.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r1.anchor: فقال الفراء والزهراوي معناه: وإن لم تنفع، فاقتصر على القسم الواحد لدلالته على الثاني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r2.claim: Some rhetoricians take the phrase as an aside reproaching Quraysh: would a reminder benefit these defiant people?
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r2.anchor: وقال بعض الحذاق: إنما قوله إن نفعت الذكرى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r3.claim: A poem illustrates this reproach: one has spoken to the living, but the addressee is unresponsive as if lifeless.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r3.anchor: لقد أسمعت لو ناديت حيا ... ولكن لا حياة لمن تنادي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r13.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r13.claim: Mujahid says the reminder is the Qur’an.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r14.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r14.claim: Ibn Shajarah says the reminder is of God, through hope and fear.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r14.anchor: بالله رغبة ورهبة , قاله ابن شجرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r15.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r15.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam reads if the reminder benefits as if the reminder is accepted.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r15.anchor: يعني إن قبلت الذكرى وهو معنى قول يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r16.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r16.claim: Ibn Shajarah takes in as since or when: reminder is always beneficial, so the verse does not make its benefit doubtful.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r16.anchor: لأن الذكرى نافعة بكل حال , قاله ابن شجرة .

TABATABAI:87:1-19/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r8.claim: The surah purifies the Prophet's speech from overt or subtle shirk, then promises preserved recitation and ease before commanding reminder.
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r8.anchor: فبدئ أولا بإصلاح كلامه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وتجريده عن كل ما يشعر بجلي الشرك

TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r2.claim: The reminder command follows the preparation, preserved recitation, and ease necessary for the mission.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r2.anchor: تفريع على ما تقدم من أمره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بتنزيه اسم ربه

TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r3.claim: The benefit condition is real: reminders are not futile and benefit the fearful by inclining them toward truth.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r3.anchor: فإنها إذا لم تنفع كانت لغوا وهو تعالى يجل عن أن يأمر باللغو

TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r4.claim: For the wretched the first reminder completes the proof and leads to avoidance; more reminders do not benefit, so turn away.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r4.anchor: والتذكرة للأشقى الذي لا خشية في قلبه لأول مرة تفيد تمام الحجة

TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r5.claim: Some say the condition is only formal because reminders always increase obedience; others take ‘if’ as ‘certainly’ or ‘when.’
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r5.anchor: وقيل الشرط شرط صوري غير حقيقي وإنما هو اخبار عن أن الذكرى نافعة

TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r6.claim: The author rejects universal benefit: reminders cannot move those who persist in defiance after the proof is complete.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#4/r6.anchor: وفيه أن كون الذكرى نافعة مفيدة دائما حتى فيمن يعاند الحق

THALABI:v10p184/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p184/r7.claim: The Prophet should admonish with Quran where it benefits; the one who fears God will take heed.
THALABI:v10p184/r7.anchor: فذكر عظ بالقرآن إن نفعت الذكرى التذكر سيذكر سيتعظ من يخشى الله
